method: Desqueezed width = recorded width x squeeze factor; recorded height and the total pixel count do not change. The display aspect ratio is the desqueezed width divided by the recorded height, reduced to its smallest whole-number ratio (5120 x 2160 reduces to 64:27), and the pixel aspect ratio a clip needs in an editor or grader is the squeeze factor itself, 4/3 = 1.333 for the factor sold as 1.33x. Ratios whose reduced terms exceed 99 are reported as a two-decimal ratio instead (2.84:1) so that unusual frames stay readable. The optional delivery check compares the frame's display aspect with a target: the stretch needed is target aspect x recorded height / recorded width, and the frame is reported as matching within 1%, close within 5%, or missing beyond that, with the signed percentage it lands narrow or wide. Known pairings that the results reproduce: 4:3 (1.33x) on 16:9 gives 2.37:1, 2x on 4:3 gives 2.67:1, 2x on 16:9 gives 3.56:1 and 1.5x on DCI 1.90 gives 2.84:1. The calculation assumes a single uniform horizontal squeeze applied to the whole frame, square sampled pixels in the desqueezed result, no sensor windowing or scaling on the way in, and a frame that already has its black bars removed. It does not inspect a file, so the recorded dimensions must come from the clip properties; real adapters vary by a per cent or two around their nominal factor, focus breathing can shift the apparent squeeze across a focus pull, and vertical anamorphic or rotated-sensor footage needs its own orientation. Inputs are limited to whole-pixel dimensions of 64-16384 px and squeeze factors of 1-3; blank, non-numeric, fractional-pixel and out-of-range values are rejected with an actionable message. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
